role: a different barrier from the one this project's conditions are about. Used as a nearest-neighbour comparison set, so a library can be told whether it resembles brain-penetrant chemistry rather than what was asked for. Never used to screen with the eNTRy conditions: a request pointing those at this data stops, and names the barrier on both sides before it does. With --yes it prints the same reasons and runs, which this sentence did not say until a request pointing the eNTRy conditions at this library was actually tried -- see contraindication 116.

paper.title: A curated diverse molecular database of blood-brain barrier permeability with chemical descriptors
paper.authors: Meng, Fanwang; Xi, Yang; Huang, Jinfeng; Ayers, Paul W.

license.name: CC0 1.0 Universal
license.verified_from: the repository's own licence declaration on github.com/theochem/B3DB, read 2026-10-14
license.note: CC0 imposes no attribution obligation. The citation above is kept because citing a dataset is the convention of the field, not because the licence requires it. This is the least restricted of the datasets here: no share-alike, as ChEMBL src_id=40 has, and no non-commercial clause, as the Scientific Reports 2025 tables had.

files.provenance_unresolved: this file matches no upstream ref. B3DB/B3DB_regression.tsv is touched by two commits -- 0ec04a3ffb1b (421,902 bytes) and 6017a837f046 (378,224 bytes) -- and the copy here is 378,970 bytes with sha256 b0f4c844..., which is neither. Measured 2026-10-16. It is not fetched and not ingested by py/fetch.py for that reason, and nothing in this repository reads it: `grep -rn B3DB_regression py/ tests/` is empty. It stays declared here because a file that was taken in and never resolved is worth recording as such.

which_version_this_is.finding: the classification file here is byte-identical to every upstream ref that has ever held it
which_version_this_is.how: measured 2026-10-16 rather than inferred. B3DB/B3DB_classification.tsv is touched by exactly one commit in the repository's history (0ec04a3ffb1b, 2021-02-25), and the file fetched at that commit, at v1.1.1 and at HEAD is the same 2,635,683 bytes with the same sha256 47a160ae... as the copy here.
which_version_this_is.withdrawn: this field previously read 'the copy here is from BEFORE upstream v1.0.0', and concluded that re-fetching 'would change the row count by 175 and move every number measured from this set'. That was inferred from one sentence of the upstream README -- 'categorical ... (7807 compounds prior to v1.0.0 and 7982 compounds after)' -- and the inference was wrong: the 7,982 does not describe this file, which holds 7,807 rows at every ref. The claim was never checked against the bytes, and it was reaching the screen: a run printed 'upstream version before v1.0.0: 7,807 rows against the 7,982 the repository holds today' as a provenance caveat to the reader. Contraindication 112.
which_version_this_is.consequence: re-fetching is safe and reproducible, which is what py/fetch.py does. The pin is the tag v1.1.1 and the guarantee is the checksum, not the tag.

counts_reconciled.classification: 7,807 rows = 4,956 BBB+ plus 2,851 BBB-, which is the split the paper reports. py/descriptors.py drops 2 rows, both BBB-, leaving 7,805 = 4,956 + 2,849. The output says 7,805 because that is the set the comparison reads.
counts_reconciled.regression: UNRESOLVED. The README states 1,058 compounds with numerical logBB; this file holds 1,063 rows. The 5-row difference is not explained. The regression file is not read by anything in the product path, so the discrepancy is recorded rather than chased.

why_this_manifest_exists_now: The two B3DB files sat in data/raw/ with no manifest while six other datasets had one, so their source and licence were recorded nowhere. It surfaced during an inventory of what could be handed to a third party: a file whose terms are unknown cannot be shipped, and a file whose terms are CC0 can. Writing it also fixed the version question, which nobody had asked.

evidence.why: the categorical BBB+/BBB- set, which is what the nearest-set comparison reads. The regression file is not evidence for any question this tool answers and the descriptor and feature derivatives are the same rows again.
